firewall.heading: Firewall
firewall.subtitle: What this host lets through, who it is currently refusing, and who it will never refuse.
firewall.sshNote: The accepts the panel renders for SSH and for its own port are not listed here and cannot be removed from this screen. Which port SSH listens on is a host fact the panel holds and does not send to the browser, so read the port yourself before changing a rule.

presets.heading: Presets
presets.subtitle: The ports opened often enough that typing them into three fields is friction. Each one sends the same request the form below sends.

rules.heading: Rules
rules.emptyDescription: Nothing has been opened from the panel. SSH and the panel's own port answer regardless — the agent renders those accepts itself, and they are not shown here.

errors.sourceInvalid: Enter a range in CIDR notation with no bits set below the prefix — 203.0.113.0/24, not 203.0.113.7/24.

form.hint: 0.0.0.0/0 admits every source. A narrower range is confirmed before it is installed.

lockout.allowWarning: This rule admits only the range shown. If it names the port your SSH daemon listens on, it replaces the unconditional accept that is holding your session open — and everybody outside that range, you included, stops reaching it.
lockout.denyWarning: Removing a rule changes what reaches this host. If this is the rule restricting SSH, the panel's unconditional accept comes back and SSH answers every source again; if it is not, the port it names stops answering.
lockout.lastRuleForPort: This leaves no rule at all for that port.
lockout.sshPortUnknown: This screen is not told which port your SSH daemon listens on: the panel holds that fact and does not send it to the browser. Read the port above before you confirm.

bans.heading: Bans
bans.subtitle: The addresses this host is refusing, and why each one is refused. The reason is the panel's own record — the kernel keeps none.
bans.emptyDescription: The brute-force detector has banned nobody, and no address has been banned by hand.

errors.durationInvalid: Enter a whole number of minutes between 1 and 525600, or leave the field empty.

form.hint: Leave the minutes empty for a ban that lasts until somebody lifts it.

whitelist.heading: Never banned
whitelist.subtitle: The ranges the automatic bans never touch.
whitelist.seedNote: On a fresh server the panel adds one row itself: the address the installer was run from, so a mistyped password cannot lock out the person who installed the panel. Nothing on the wire marks that row as the panel's — its note is what says so — and removing the range you administer from is how an operator locks themselves out.
whitelist.tableCaption: Ranges exempt from the automatic bans
whitelist.confirmRemove: Remove this exemption? The automatic bans can reach the range again — and if it is the range you administer from, that includes you.
whitelist.emptyDescription: Every address can be banned, including the one you are reading this from.

errors.cidrInvalid: Enter a range in CIDR notation with no bits set below the prefix — 203.0.113.0/24, not 203.0.113.7/24.
errors.noteTooLong: The note is longer than 200 characters.

form.hint: Say what the range is. In six months the note is the only thing that will explain the row.
